audit.whatIsWrong: Sejuani wins only 46.17% over 392 games, yet the chart gave her the two-item stage and Nautilus nothing at all — six Skill rows and one Sejuani row.
audit.why: Packet defect confirmed. A losing matchup that never concedes a single stage is unreadable. The prose already describes Nautilus owning the opening — Staggering Blow's root, the Dredge Line threat, no Frost stacks and no stun to answer with — so levels 1-3 belong to him. Level 6 is a genuine Sejuani flip because Glacial Prison reaches 1300 against Dredge Line's 1150. The item stages are two tanks who cannot kill each other, which is Skill, and with the largest sample in my slice at 392 games a 46.17% is a real if narrow loss.
audit.corrected: win[] becomes Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Skill, Sejuani, Skill, Skill with matching phase sides and ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike described Nautilus's abilities by slot letter only — 'his passive root', 'his Q hook', 'his E slow into W shield bash'.
audit.why: Packet defect: the matchup never named Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide or Depth Charge once. Worse, the level 1-2 spike said the passive 'procs on every auto'. Riot's text is 'Nautilus' FIRST Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly' — first attack per target, not every auto. That difference decides whether stepping up for a second W arc is safe.
audit.corrected: Spikes and whys now use the real names and the real passive behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The range comparison that carries the whole level-6 plan was written as 'outranges his Q by a full spell-cast length'.
audit.why: Glacial Prison is 1300 range; Dredge Line is 1150. That is a real 150-unit edge and it is the reason the level-6 flip exists — but 'a full spell-cast length' is not a number a player can stand at. Riptide is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, both previously unnamed.
audit.corrected: Both ranges stated, Riptide and Titan's Wrath named with cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. breakdown.cooldowns said only 'count it out loud if you must'.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — the single window the lane turns on. Depth Charge is 120/100/80s against Glacial Prison's 120/105/90s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added with the sequencing rule: step up after a missed Dredge Line, not before.

edits.after: Staggering Blow roots you on his FIRST attack, and Dredge Line (14s at rank 1) reaches 1150 — he punishes face-tanks before your stun exists.

edits.before: Stack Frost with W's double-strike from near-max range, then trigger E stun before his passive root procs
edits.after: Stack Frost with Winter's Wrath at its 600 range, then fire Permafrost before Riptide's slow lands

edits.after: Layer Riptide's slow into Titan's Wrath (12s shield) to outlast Winter's Wrath before Permafrost

edits.after: Staggering Blow roots you on his first attack and you have no Frost stacks or stun ready at Level 1 — stay out of his auto range entirely and let him push.

edits.before: Glacial Prison outranges his Q by a full spell-cast length — throw R first on his hook cooldown and he cannot hook-cancel you before the blizzard lands.
edits.after: Glacial Prison reaches 1300 against Dredge Line's 1150 — throw R first on his hook cooldown, from the one step outside the range he can answer from.

edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Q): 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — his only real engage, so step up after it misses, never before. - Riptide (E): 7s down to 5s. - Titan's Wrath (W): flat 12s shield. - Depth Charge (R): 120/100/80s.

notes: UNVERIFIED and deliberately left in place rather than restated: three separate lines (spikes[3], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], whys[1], content.early) claim Dredge Line can 'interrupt your Q charge mid-dash' and 'cancel your engage'. Dredge Line does pull both champions together, and Arctic Assault is a charge, but whether a displacement interrupts an in-progress charge is not in Riot's text and is exactly the class of thing these files say is unknown. I did not repeat the claim in any line I wrote, and I did not delete it either. It should be checked on the League Wiki before the next pass, because four separate pieces of advice on this page depend on it. Chart change is the largest judgement call in my slice — 392 games at 46.17% is a real loss, and a chart that conceded nothing to Nautilus was the flagged defect.
